Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Russia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The website <https://www.tv5monde.com> ceased to exist, it redirects to the site <https://www.tv5mondeplus.com>.

yt-dlp can't download videos from the site <https://www.tv5mondeplus.com> now.

Will it be possible to download from the website <https://www.tv5mondeplus.com> ?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

United States

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So I am trying to download a video from NBC, and I keep getting this error : [NBC] 9000245499: Unable to download JSON metadata: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden (caused by <HTTPError 403: Forbidden>)  
`  
I have tried to apply fixes of the other 403 error issues I have seen but they are for other sites and it till doesn't work

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required

<https://www.playsuisse.ch/watch/4043540?episodeId=4072865>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Hello.

While downloading episodes of a series from PlaySuisse, I noticed that the extractor already discovers multiple subtitle playlists per language, but yt-dlp currently collapses them into a single selectable subtitle language, making one dowloadable and the others, as far as I could tell, unreachable via normal CLI options.

This is not a DRM issue; all subtitle URLs are already available to the extractor.

# What happens

For some PlaySuisse episodes, listing subtitles reports--e.g.,
    
    
    Language Formats
    fr vtt, vtt
    it vtt, vtt
    de vtt, vtt
    

Dumping JSON metadata shows that this corresponds to two distinct HLS subtitle playlists per language, for example (Italian):
    
    
    "subtitles": {
      "it": [
        {
          "url": "https://stipo2-vod-prod.akamaized.net/stipo.../index-f11.m3u8",
          "ext": "vtt",
          "protocol": "m3u8_native"
        },
        {
          "url": "https://stipo2-vod-prod.akamaized.net/stipo.../index-f12.m3u8",
          "ext": "vtt",
          "protocol": "m3u8_native"
        }
      ],
      "fr": [
    

These are genuinely different subtitle tracks (different text content) visible in the PlaySuisse web player (at least, in many cases I see one I wish in the web player and another one downloaded).

However, yt-dlp currently

  * selects only one subtitle track per language and

  * provides no way to request the second track via sub-langs or all-subs.




# Expected / desired behavior

Expose multiple subtitle tracks per language as distinct subtitle IDs, so that users can explicitly select them.

For example, instead of keeping both tracks under a single language key (e.g., it: track1 + track2), emit different "languages" (e.g., it: track1, it-1: track2).

This would allow selecting both--e.g.,
    
    
    yt-dlp --sub-langs it,it-1 --write-subs --embed-subs URL
    

No yt-dlp core changes are needed.

# Why this seems safe

  * The extractor already has all necessary information (URLs, protocol, ext).

  * This affects only PlaySuisse subtitles.

  * Default behavior remains unchanged (users still get one subtitle, at random but this is so today, unless they explicitly ask for more).

  * Similar language-suffix patterns are already used in other extractors, I am told from ChatGPT.




# Example URL (for testing)

<https://www.playsuisse.ch/watch/4043540?episodeId=4072865>

There should be six subtitles (two per national language) and there are only three (see run below).

Thanks for maintaining yt-dlp and playsuisse.py!

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I personally experienced it on [S1E5](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/m0021k8t/daddy-issues-series-1-5-man-mess) and [S1E6](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/m0021k8x/daddy-issues-series-1-6-sadie) of Daddy Issues (all of the other episodes of both seasons have no issues).

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I have been successfully download videos from watch ESPN or ESPN+ for a while, but this has recently stopped working. Typically I run the command 'yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser firefox "<https://www.espn.com/watch/player/_/id/a3c7ec29-f4c0-46e9-a537-276f0c2675cf>"'. This will successfully using the cookies from firefox for authentication and then start the download. This portion still works correctly. However, after starting the download it immediately gets a response of 410: Gone.

I have tried uninstalling yt-dlp, updating, updating python, etc but continue to receive the same error.

## Description

[](https://github.com/trainman261)

[trainman261](https://github.com/trainman261)

opened [on Jan 16, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15584#issue-3819925846)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

For some reason, CBC has borked their JSON formatting in the CBC Player. Their player processes it without any issues, but even the lenient JSON parser throws its hands up. The problem is it has a number of sections like this:  
`"insertAd":undefined`  
which AFAIK is not valid JSON. For myself I've made a hacky solution by just adding the following line after the webpage is downloaded (about line 400):  
`webpage = webpage.replace(':undefined', ':"undefined"')`  
And suddenly everything works again.  
At the moment I don't have time to implement a proper fix, but I hope this can help someone solve the problem without too much further effort.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

US

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So I'm pretty sure this was under the nbc extractor, but USANetwork finally transitioned over to Versant and updated the website so now it shows as unsupported.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

USA

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Previously working on the site, it now does not work to download with the error `no video formats found`. See below log.

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

United States of America

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Up until about 2 weeks ago, downloads from Xiaohongshu.com were in the highest quality but since then I've only been able to download at a max resolution of 1080p. I verified by re-downloading a video I previously downloaded in 4K; the video now only downloads in 1080p.

For all I know, Xiaohongshu are clamping down on source-quality downloads so this might not be something yt-dlp can fix.

The verbose output below is for a video where I'm not sure if the original was in 4K quality.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Any

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Yesterday `yt-dlp -J "https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=312304267031140"` worked, today it errors with:
    
    
    ERROR: [facebook:ads] 312304267031140: Unable to download webpage: HTTP Error 403: Client challenge (caused by <HTTPError 403: Client challenge>)
    

* * *

Challenge flow & bypass:

  1. navigate to the page, and you are presented with


    
    
    $ curl https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=312304267031140
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
    <head>
    <title>Ad Library</title>
    </head>
    <body>
    <script>
    
    (function() {
      if (document.readyState !== 'loading') {
        executeChallenge();
      } else {
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', executeChallenge);
      }
      function executeChallenge() {
        fetch('/__rd_verify_Q_6hBQNhbQK82SnvsYkd-8VYF8YZIN4SEe01HeAKLLr0Jk2_gA?challenge=3', {
          method: 'POST',
        })
        .finally(() => window.location.reload());
      }
    })();
    
    </script>
    </body>
    </html>
    

  2. fetch `https://www.facebook.com/__rd_verify_....` and you get a `set-cookie` header


    
    
    $ curl -I https://www.facebook.com/__rd_verify_Q_6hBQNhbQK82SnvsYkd-8VYF8YZIN4SEe01HeAKLLr0Jk2_gA?challenge=3
    HTTP/2 200
    set-cookie: rd_challenge=Q_6hBQP6qJZ1mDL1OAyXes1k3cZkcukvYZZrpKwJ2hiArlRZflBtw_uutpL7s_FqnRqggY3cdEEg3NMYy9hb92evVG0; Max-Age=86400; Domain=facebook.com; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
    content-type: text/plain
    content-length: 0
    server: proxygen-bolt
    x-fb-connection-quality: GOOD; q=0.7, rtt=79, rtx=0, c=10, mss=1380, tbw=3590, tp=-1, tpl=-1, uplat=0, ullat=-1
    alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400
    date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 19:16:29 GMT
    

  3. pass `rd_challenge` cookie to the original request and it works now


    
    
    $ curl -I https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=312304267031140 -H "cookie: rd_challenge=Q_6hBQP6qJZ1mDL1OAyXes1k3cZkcukvYZZrpKwJ2hiArlRZflBtw_uutpL7s_FqnRqggY3cdEEg3NMYy9hb92evVG0;" | grep -i HTTP | head -1
      % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                     Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed
      0     0    0     0    0     0      0      0 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:--     0
    HTTP/2 200
    
    
    
    yt-dlp -J "https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=719057414376082" --add-headers "cookie: rd_challenge=Q_6hBQP6qJZ1mDL1OAyXes1k3cZkcukvYZZrpKwJ2hiArlRZflBtw_uutpL7s_FqnRqggY3cdEEg3NMYy9hb92evVG0;" | jq
    
    {
      "title": "Cozy Season is here!",
      "uploader": "Casper",
      "uploader_id": "224110981099062",
      "uploader_url": "https://www.facebook.com/Casper/",
      "timestamp": 1768328401,
      "like_count": 628940,
      "entries": [...

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

America

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Videos from Disney download fine and subtitle files are generated when I add "--write-sub", but the subtitle file content is not subtitles, it is some XML code containing an error, like this:  
`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><xml><result><error><objectType>KalturaAPIException</objectType><code>INVALID_KS</code><message>Invalid KS &quot;EXPIRED&quot;, Error &quot;-1,INVALID_STR&quot;</message><args><item><objectType>KalturaApiExceptionArg</objectType><name>KSID</name><value>EXPIRED</value></item><item><objectType>KalturaApiExceptionArg</objectType><name>ERR_CODE</name><value>-1</value></item><item><objectType>KalturaApiExceptionArg</objectType><name>ERR_DESC</name><value>INVALID_STR</value></item></args></error></result><executionTime>0.0072848796844482</executionTime></xml>`

I tried it with several videos, for example:  
<https://video.disney.com/watch/forces-of-destiny-teaser-552f38efb45a8a8d49483b10>  
<https://video.disney.com/watch/star-wars-forces-of-destiny-volume-1-disney-55c041c3318b07cf2bb99b82>  
<https://video.disney.com/watch/star-wars-forces-of-destiny-volume-2-disney-567f0bb335fea2cca5a11bc2>

Watching the videos in a browser, I can see there are in fact subtitles when I click on the CC button of their player.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[](https://github.com/Spike1377)

opened [on Jul 4, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13633#issue-3202011679)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Australia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I would like to download video with audio descriptions off ABC iview, so I used `./yt-dlp_linux https://iview.abc.net.au/video/CO2002V001S00 --audio-multistreams ` but no luck it doesn't get the described sound, just the regular sound without the describer. I also tried it with default settings.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    [anthony@archlinux tmp]$ echo test < output
    bash: output: No such file or directory
    [anthony@archlinux tmp]$ echo test > output
    [anthony@archlinux tmp]$ ./yt-dlp_linux -vU  https://iview.abc.net.au/video/CO2002V001S00 --audio-multistreams > output.txt
    [debug] Command-line config: ['-vU', 'https://iview.abc.net.au/video/CO2002V001S00', '--audio-multistreams']
    [debug] Encodings: locale UTF-8, fs utf-8, pref UTF-8, out utf-8 (No ANSI), error utf-8, screen utf-8 (No ANSI)
    [debug] yt-dlp version stable@2025.06.30 from yt-dlp/yt-dlp (linux_exe)

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Hi, with yt-dlp you can monitored the channel every couple of minutes, but after one live stream downloaded the command stop, and you have to manually execute the command again. Is there any way of automatically -repeat (monitoring channel command) with yt-dlp that doesn't involve batching?

Thanks

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[site-enhancementFeature request for some website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-enhancement%22)Feature request for some website

## Description

[](https://github.com/adenry)

[adenry](https://github.com/adenry)

opened [on Jan 26, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12201#issue-2811585629)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I am batch downloading a bunch (hundreds) of videos from a website with yt-dlp, also downloading their thumbnails and embedding them in the video files. Everything works great.

However, the website is using URL width and height parameters to make the thumbnails smaller. I.e. a thumbnail link looks like this:  
`image.jpeg?height=354&region=0%2C0%2C1920%2C1080&width=630`

It would be great if yt-dlp had a feature to be able to ignore those width, height and region parameters and download the original thumbnail file, but as far as I know, it doesn't (please correct me if I am wrong).

So I would like to ask if it is possible (and if so - how) to do the following:

  1. Use yt-dlp to quickly download just the .json files for a bunch of videos
  2. I will then edit those files using Notepad++ to remove the thumbnail width and height parameters
  3. Somehow use yt-dlp to download the videos using the edited json files



Is this possible?

Or is there any other way that I can download the original thumbnail files and also embed them in the video files?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

<https://www.starwars.com/video/trailer-the-bad-batch>

Videos can be successfully downloaded from starwars.com using the Firefox extension Video DownloadHelper, but I prefer and need to use yt-dlp.

Consider checking YouTube extractor before PeerTube by default#15594

[#15596](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/15596)

Copy link

Labels

[bugBug that is not site-specific](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22bug%22)Bug that is not site-specific

[](https://github.com/ndren)

## Description

[](https://github.com/ndren)

[ndren](https://github.com/ndren)

opened [on Jan 16, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15594#issue-3823847946)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

As shown in the profiler below (pyinstrument), checking PeerTube.suitable is very expensive due to the large number of instances it has to chew through and re.compile.  
[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/59375667/537031994-9eb337af-a019-4629-8271-549450458609.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..LWUNlh-nKrwJ4PZHKZGGmo0bV-vuJn8sBYJlQo1FguQ)

Technically it makes sense to check the extractors in alphabetical order, but would it make sense to somehow make an exception and check youtube first, if the url is something like youtube.com or youtu.be? Often users use youtube as an extractor for yt-dlp.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

N/A

I've worked around the issue on my end by setting `--use-extractors 'youtube,all'`, but it would be nice to have this as a default (or at least better documented).

## Description

[](https://github.com/LillyMoon42)

[LillyMoon42](https://github.com/LillyMoon42)

opened [on Jan 1, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15461#issue-3774765508)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When using the argument sponsorblock-remove to remove segments, the video is trimmed correctly but the audio remains. Playing this back results in differing behaviour depending on the video player; VLC mostly handles it well, though the audio skips a bit, but MPC-BE pauses the video stream whilst the audio catches up, resulting in the segment not being skipped at all.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The issue is basically whenever the web_safari player is used for youtube links, sometimes it returns m3u8 links, and if you force convert to mkv,

The smallest command i was able to reproduce is with this
    
    
    $ yt-dlp -vU --format 'bv*+ba[format_note*=original]/bv*+ba/b' --format-sort vcodec:h264,res,acodec:aac --embed-metadata --merge-output-format mkv --remux-video mkv --extractor-args "youtube:player-client=web_safari;formats=incomplete" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54OKrOYuFIc

running the merge manually also result in error

## Description

[](https://github.com/McCio)

[McCio](https://github.com/McCio)

opened [on Nov 1, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14869#issue-3578563529)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Hi, it seems bug [#3557](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3557) resurfaced during last month, but linked to `f.close()` instead of `f.truncate()`.  
The context is when writing to the archive file that is in a mounted filesystem via rclone w/cache, so I guess it is a filesystem that doesn't allow seeks.  
I think this bug is different than [#3557](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3557) as it is happening during `f.close()`, meaning the archive file wouldn't be updated if the error gets ignored as it was done during `f.truncate()`.

I confirmed that pointing to my local filesystem the same command succeeds.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

latvia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I record live stream from tiktok which requires login. I use cookie from browser. When i start recording in CMD is written:  
F:\yt-dlp>yt-dlp --cookies=cookies.txt <https://www.tiktok.com/@username/live>  
[tiktok:live] Extracting URL: <https://www.tiktok.com/@username/live>  
[tiktok:live] username: Downloading webpage  
[tiktok:live] 7585166667379510017: Downloading JSON metadata  
[tiktok:live] 7585166667379510017: Downloading JSON metadata  
[info] 7585166667379510017: Downloading 1 format(s): flv-origin  
[download] Destination: MF 2025-12-18 15_09 [7585166667379510017].flv  
[download] 389.93MiB at 152.30KiB/s (00:43:42)  
then came:  
[download] 708.92MiB at 162.71KiB/s (01:14:22)[download] Got error: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='pull-w5-sg01.fcdn.eu.tiktokcdn.com', port=443): Read timed out.. Retrying (1/10)...  
after it yt-dlp deleted file which was recorded and started to write video into new file.  
I.e. on every disconnect yt-dlp deletes file.  
I use newest nightly 2025.12.15.233113 version.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    F:\yt-dlp>yt-dlp --cookies=cookies.txt https://www.tiktok.com/@username/live
    [tiktok:live] Extracting URL: https://www.tiktok.com/@username/live
    [tiktok:live] username: Downloading webpage
    [tiktok:live] 7585166667379510017: Downloading JSON metadata
    [tiktok:live] 7585166667379510017: Downloading JSON metadata
    [info] 7585166667379510017: Downloading 1 format(s): flv-origin
    [download] Destination: MF 2025-12-18 15_09 [7585166667379510017].flv
    [download]  389.93MiB at  152.30KiB/s (00:43:42)
    [download]  708.92MiB at  162.71KiB/s (01:14:22)[download] Got error: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='pull-w5-sg01.fcdn.eu.tiktokcdn.com', port=443): Read timed out.. Retrying (1/10)...

## Description

[](https://github.com/ARandomGitGuy)

[ARandomGitGuy](https://github.com/ARandomGitGuy)

opened [on Jan 10, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15534#issue-3799670242)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

when using the `--paths` options to set the `home` and `temp` directories, if the `temp` directory is set to a `tmpfs` mounted filesystem (RAM drive, for example) at the end of the process, the cleanup of the temporary file is left behind with what appears to be a permissions error

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

**Problem:**  
When using `aria2c` as an external downloader with `yt-dlp`, interrupted downloads do **not resume from where they stopped** on the next run. With the native downloader, yt-dlp resumes fine, but `aria2c` does not seem to behave the same.

### What I Expect

I want `aria2c` to continue downloading a partially downloaded video file automatically on the second run—basically the same resume behavior that yt-dlp’s built-in downloader provides.

### What I Have Tried

I already have a **locally configured`aria2c` instance** that correctly resumes interrupted downloads. However, when I run `aria2c` through yt-dlp (even after passing my config via `--downloader-args`), it still does **not** resume the file properly.

Here is my yt-dlp config where I try to pass downloader arguments to aria2c:  
[The part of yt-dlp option--downloader-args](https://github.com/pritam12426/dotfile/blob/28fa01539da902dd9ecb6ba6fa2d89a2da995e05/dirwin_os/config/yt-dlp/config#L110-L121)

### Bonus / Reference

Here is my local `aria2c` configuration that correctly resumes interrupted downloads outside of yt-dlp:  
[~/.config/aria2/aria2.conf](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pritam12426/dotfile/refs/heads/main/dirwin_os/config/aria2/aria2.conf)

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The following embedded yt_dlp will crash with
    
    
    yt_dlp.networking.exceptions.RequestError: Impersonate target "" is not available. See --list-impersonate-targets for available targets. This request requires browser impersonation, however you may be missing dependencies required to support this target.
    

when executed by `threading` while the "ordinary" execution on `download()` works just fine.
    
    
    #!/usr/bin/env python
    
    import threading
    import yt_dlp
    
    URL="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TsXMe8H6iyc"
    
    def download():
    
            ydl_opts = {
                "ignoreerrors": True,
                "writesubtitles": True,
                "subtitleslangs": ["sv.*"],
                "outtmpl": "/tmp/data/%(uploader)s/%(timestamp)s/S01E%(upload_date)s - %(uploader)s - %(title)s [%(id)s].%(ext)s",
                 "verbose": True,
            }
            with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(ydl_opts) as ydl:
                info = ydl.extract_info(URL,download=True)
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
            download()
            z = threading.Thread(target=download)
            z.start()

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

When I use `--embed-metadata` (and `--parse-metadata`), Explorer on my pc doesn't show some metadata such as comment (URL).  
[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/142886283/508541184-fad622e9-57eb-44b2-ac4b-91876cf5ecbe.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJnaXRodWIuY29tIiwiYXVkIjoicmF3LmdpdGh1YnVzZXJjb250ZW50LmNvbSIsImtleSI6ImtleTUiLCJleHAiOjE3Njg3MDAwNzQsIm5iZiI6MTc2ODY5OTc3NCwicGF0aCI6Ii8xNDI4ODYyODMvNTA4NTQxMTg0LWZhZDYyMmU5LTU3ZWItNDRiMi1hYzRiLTkxODc2Y2Y1ZWNiZS5wbmc_.Gw9sdOdgl2bk0AokTJnQVvbjaQQ0kTPYx7aMRcD30ug)  
That on one pc does show but only first 30 letters.  
[](https://camo.githubusercontent.) (with `--parse-metadata "Deltarune Takeover;`nThe Amazing Digital Circus - Main Theme;:(?s)(?P<meta_comment>.+)"`)

# If m3u8 subtitles are linked in a playlist without an extension of .m3u8, downloads fail - patch available #14529

[New issue](/login?return_to=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14529)

[New issue](/login?return_to=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14529)

Open

If m3u8 subtitles are linked in a playlist without an extension of .m3u8, downloads fail - patch available#14529

Copy link

## Description

[](https://github.com/atrottmann)

[atrottmann](https://github.com/atrottmann)

opened [on Oct 2, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14529#issue-3479062561)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Apparently, at least one commercially available HLS packager generates .m3u8 files that refer to subtitle playlists without an extension.

Those .m3u8 files look somewhat like this:
    
    
    #EXTM3U
    #EXT-X-VERSION:7
    #EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS
    #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO,GROUP-ID="AACL",NAME="audio_482_deu",LANGUAGE="deu",AUTOSELECT=YES,DEFAULT=YES,CHANNELS="2",URI="stuff.m3u8/Alter-audio_482_deu(482)"
    #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO,GROUP-ID="AACL",NAME="audio_483_eng",LANGUAGE="eng",AUTOSELECT=YES,DEFAULT=NO,CHANNELS="2",URI="stuff.m3u8/Alter-audio_483_eng(483)"
    #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=SUBTITLES,GROUP-ID="subtitle",NAME="deu_0",LANGUAGE="deu",AUTOSELECT=YES,DEFAULT=NO,FORCED=NO,URI="stuff.m3u8/Vtt-deu_0(100)"
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=1000000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2,avc1.4d401e",RESOLUTION=768x432,FRAME-RATE=25,AUDIO="AACL",SUBTITLES="subtitle"
    stuff.m3u8/Level(1)
    #EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=115195,CODECS="avc1.4d401e",RESOLUTION=768x432,URI="stuff.m3u8/Iframe(1)"
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=7200000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2,avc1.64002a",RESOLUTION=1920x1080,FRAME-RATE=50,AUDIO="AACL",SUBTITLES="subtitle"
    stuff.m3u8/Level(2)
    #EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=336245,CODECS="avc1.64002a",RESOLUTION=1920x1080,URI="stuff.m3u8/Iframe(2)"
    #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=96000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2",AUDIO="AACL",SUBTITLES="subtitle"
    stuff.m3u8/Level(3)
    

When `yt-dlp` parses the .m3u8 file, the function `extract_media` in `yt_dlp/extractor/common.py` under the `if media_type == 'SUBTITLES':` case runs `determine_ext(url)`.

When this runs with a "normal" URL like `https://server/path/stuff/Vtt-deu0(100).m3u8`, this determines an extension of "m3u8", and the following `if sub_info['ext'] == 'm3u8':` matches. This then eventually results in subtitles that are downloaded correctly.

However, because _here_ the URL looks like `https://server/path/stuff.m3u8/Vtt-deu_0(100)`, `determine_ext` returns an extension of "unknown_video" and the download proceeds with "Invoking http downloader" to downloading "this link", which then downloads the playlist, not the subtitles.

I'm not sure if it is actually necessary to run `determine_ext` here, because we are already in a HLS stream and I woudln't know what other kind of extension could be used. Just to be safe I changed the call to `determine_ext` by adding a default value of "m3u8", resulting in the following diff:
    
    
    diff --git a/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py b/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    index 573a9c5a0..ee0fb0ca3 100644
    --- a/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    +++ b/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    @@ -2292,7 +2292,7 @@ def extract_media(x_media_line):
                     url = format_url(media['URI'])
                     sub_info = {
                         'url': url,
    -                    'ext': determine_ext(url),
    +                    'ext': determine_ext(url, default_ext='m3u8'),
                     }
                     if sub_info['ext'] == 'm3u8':
                         # Per RFC 8216 §3.1, the only possible subtitle format m3u8

This makes it work for the streams that I tested and shouldn't break anything.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/Black-Platypus)

[Black-Platypus](https://github.com/Black-Platypus)

opened [on Nov 26, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15175#issue-3669110008)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

(Same as outlined in [#15039](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15039) \- apologies for bad sites in log)  
I went on a whole tangent building a node app that could simulate all sorts of different failure cases to have control over reliable, reproducible errors. When it came to hosting it publicly, I realized I didn't have good options available. So I tried just manually making failure playlists and hosting things on my web server: That already seems enough to reproduce the case of "ERROR: Did not get any data blocks".

Compare:

  * `https://benjamin-philipp.com/streamTest/playlist.m3u8` <\-- OK: Nothing is missing, everything is fine
  * `https://benjamin-philipp.com/streamTest/fail_empty_on_5.m3u8` <\-- **Fragment 5 contains no data: Fragment is skipped after error**
  * `https://benjamin-philipp.com/streamTest/fail_notfound_on_5.m3u8` <\-- OK: Fragment 5 not found: yt-dlp retries `fragment-retries` times



I set yt-dlp to use
    
    
    {
        "retries": 5,
        "fragment-retries": 6
    }
    

, yet it seems to immediately skip fragments if it encounters the "Did not get any data blocks" error.

> fragment not found; Skipping fragment %d

It seems like yt-dlp should honor the fragment-retries setting, but the error is not caught at a low enough level(?)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

in other words, if put into opus container,

Please teach me what option I should write.  
I'm reading the modify metadata section but I don't quite understand it.

## Description

[](https://github.com/Throun)

[Throun](https://github.com/Throun)

opened [on Apr 28, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9808#issue-2267274110)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

First off, thank you for this great project!

Atomic systems like Fedora Silverblue are commonly designed around using flatpaks as the primary, if not only, way of installing software, leaving users unable to use yt-dlp. There are some graphical programs available on Flathub that use yt-dlp, but they are limited in how much you can do compared to the command line. I believe the project should either build a flatpak or make a submission request to Flathub to allow affected users the ability to use this software.  
Flatpak also helps provide a standardized environment for users; what works on one system should work exactly the same on another. This might help weed out issues that are from distros/users rather than the project.

I have written a preliminary manifest that someone can use as a start if there is interest:  
[downloaders.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140259/downloaders.yaml.txt)  
[org.yt_dlp.yt_dlp.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140260/org.yt_dlp.yt_dlp.yaml.txt)  
[python3-modules.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140261/python3-modules.yaml.txt)  
I am willing to answer any questions about this to the best of my ability.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

_No response_

👍React with 👍4MrRawes, tazihad, esjarc and FernandoMMuniz

# [Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels. #11084

[Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels.#11084

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question[site:youtube](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site%3Ayoutube%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/pxssy)

[pxssy](https://github.com/pxssy)

opened [on Sep 25, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11084#issue-2547768578)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Singapore

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When a youtube channel input like <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> is given to yt-dlp, it parses ALL /video and /shorts, then downloads them sequentially by chronological order, latest upload first, as its what is given by the API. Its not possible to sort in any other way.

In this case, If an option like --dateafter or --datebefore is used, many unnecessary requests are sent to youtube for videos that clearly will not match a filter.

Example

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 21001231 will match 0 videos, since the earliest video is in 2024. However it will check through EVERY video, even the ones before 2024, which is unnecessary and slow.

Similarly, yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--datebefore 00010101 will also match 0 videos, but it will check every video until the very first one.

Until youtube changes this, I believe this additional checks are not necessary at all.

Therefore I suggest 2 changes.

  1. \--datebefore runs the downloading backwards, starting from the oldest video in the channel.



EDIT: an existing workaround is -I "::-1"

  2. a switch like --date-skip 5, that skips process after it has checked 5 videos and they do not match the date requirements.



Expected behaviour should then be

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 20240101 --date-skip 3

Downloads videos after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip  
Download shorts after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip

exit

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

the Netherlands

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Example video:  
`https://banbye.com/watch/v_4iDAJIT4SfA7`

See also earlier issue [#8584](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8584), resolved by [#10332](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/10332).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Downloading a multi-audio stream, marks both audio streams as `default` (see below).

Is that expected, or an error?

Should the first respective stream only be marked as default?  
(e.g. for `137+140-0+140-1`, only `140-0` should be default)

I looked at <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc%20is%3Aissue%20--audio-multistreams>

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Having yt-dlp create a symlink for playlists with a certain path #13674

[New issue](/login?return_to=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674)

Copy link

[New issue](/login?return_to=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674)

Copy link

Open

Open

Having yt-dlp create a symlink for playlists with a certain path#13674

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

[](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

## Description

[](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

[Aces-and-Jacks](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

opened [on Jul 9, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674#issue-3214340349)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

As far as I can see, no one has posted a question like this. I know you can use the `--exec` command for symlinks. But I'm not really code savy to figure this out. This probably isn't possible but I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask.

I currently have the videos I download symlinked as `--exec 'cd "/Users/$USER/Downloads/sym-folder" && ln -s --'`. Which worked well before. All my videoes get downloaded to their own folders as `/Users/$USER/YT-Downloads/%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date>%Y-%m-%d)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s].%(ext)s'` and the resulting files get symlinked to the other directory.

The thing is when I download a playlist, a folder that shows the playlist uploader gets created along with the other uploads for each video `%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]`. Which I'm fine with (I also see in the info file the playlist name and count it was with), but for the symlinked videos they just show without any filepath order. Which would make sense based on the file path. I tried using one of the fields in the OUTPUT TEMPLATE options but that didn't work properly. I figured it probably wouldn't tho.

I had asked for help for just symlinking in the past in [#11080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11080) and based on what `bashonly` provided I tried to figure it out. He mentioned there was a field for `filepath` but I guess I had asked too many questions since he didn't answer, and I had already gotten my main question at the time answered. For symlinking he meantioned

> `ln -s -- %(filepath,_filename|)q`

but then said

> IMPORTANT: you should only ever use `%()q` in `--exec` arguments, and never `%()s`

So to sum it all up, I was wondering about a command that creates symlinks in a filepath that includes the playlist uploader. Like some sort of field string or something. I hope I didn't make this too confusing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

## Description

[](https://github.com/gwttk)

[gwttk](https://github.com/gwttk)

opened [on Apr 16, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9695#issue-2245055153)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Ok so first, `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter" --print "after_move:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s"` works fine.  
But let's skip download cuz we are just for subs. `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter" --print "after_move:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`.  
No print no postprocess.  
So I tried before_dl. `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter:when=before_dl" --print "before_dl:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`. Sub is converted but the print happened before the postprocess so the output is wrong.  
But if I move the print to post_process it won't print `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter:when=before_dl" --print "post_process:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`  
Now... what should I do, to download subs only and call the postprocessor and print the converted filename?  
Is there a stage between before_dl and post_process so I can print the result after the postprocess?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

## Description

[](https://github.com/dajotim937)

[dajotim937](https://github.com/dajotim937)

opened [on Jun 3, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13381#issue-3113644843)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So, here is related issue: [#6501](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6501)

But I'm asking not about overwriting original video file, but about final (opus in case of youtube) file that being overwritten.

Example:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcrsSaWZ4CY`  
This command download video and extract audio into 'Deja Reve.opus' file.  
Then:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata --no-overwrites "%(title)s.%(ext)s" -w https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L8M71Xu1rVc`  
And no warnings, no errors, just overwrite of final file.

Well, it's kinda hard to tell from first glance. Same track with same name and maybe yt-dlp just overwrite metadata.  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIAku-Qwfl0`  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" --no-overwrites https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBQpZsnLyMw`

Yeah, nope. End up with second track that overwrite first one. So. Is it a bug? Or intended behaviour? How to prevent such behaviour if so (except puting something like %(id)s into filename)?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Extractors: Availability of DOM query functions#10621

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/Lalufu)

[Lalufu](https://github.com/Lalufu)

opened [on Aug 1, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10621#issue-2442230799)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I am looking into writing a new extractor, and I'm wondering if I'm missing some obvious utility functions for extracting information from a HTML page. I had, maybe naively, expected there to be functions similar to `document.querySelector()` and `document.querySelectorAll()` from JS, which take a more or less abstract path through the document and return matching elements, maybe backed by `BeautifulSoup` or other libraries. I have found the `get_element_*` functions from `utils`, which don't seem to quite do the same thing (I can't seem to look for tags of a certain type?), and looking at other extractors, using regular expressions seems to be pretty popular for some reason instead. There's also some xpath support, but from a quick look nothing seems to utilize this for dealing with HTML.  
Do functions like this exist, and I haven't found them, or is this a discouraged approach for some reason?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

_No response_

# `--simulate` doesn't accurately simulate downloading under certain conditions #9843

[New issue](/login?return_to=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9843)

`--simulate` doesn't accurately simulate downloading under certain conditions#9843

[#9862](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/9862)

Copy link

Labels

[bugBug that is not site-specific](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22bug%22)Bug that is not site-specific

## Description

[](https://github.com/seproDev)

[seproDev](https://github.com/seproDev)

opened [on May 2, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9843#issue-2276339467)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When running a yt-dlp command with `--simulate` (and without an `-f` arg), the default format selection differs from an unsimulated run under any of these conditions:

  * ffmpeg is not available
  * the outtmpl is `-`
  * the URL is for a livestream (and `--live-from-start` was not passed)



A dry-run/simulate option should actually simulate the behaviour that will occur when downloading.  
This behaviour is currently undocumented. Either the behaviour should be changed or at the very least be documented.

* * *

_Copying initial discussion:[#9805 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/9805#discussion_r1588171627)_

It looks like we can trace this logic back to [ytdl-org/youtube-dl@`0017d9a`](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/commit/0017d9ad6de831384e74db14a821e4c94020c9ac)

Back then, upstream's default format spec was only `best` if ffmpeg was not available. So a simulated run would result in a "requested formats not available" error if ffmpeg was not available and there was no combined video+audio format available. This `simulate` check seems to be added so that you could print json without having to manually pass `-f bv+ba` or `-f bv` etc in this scenario -- see the linked upstream PR

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below
